A strain-gauge bridge produces microvolts per unit strain, and an Arduino's
ADC — even the well-characterized one [S1](../S1-daq-static/index.qmd)
measured — cannot resolve microvolts on its own. This experiment starts from
that arithmetic, sizes the instrumentation amplifier it demands, and then
uses it twice: once on a standalone load cell, to characterize what a static
mechanical calibration actually has to separate (linearity, hysteresis,
creep, zero drift), and once on gauges bonded to [the cantilever
beam](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd), to compare quarter, half and full bridge
wiring and to measure — not assume — what temperature compensation buys.

The beam's own dimensions are not decided (see [the beam
rig](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd#sec-beam-design)); every relation here is
symbolic in the same way, and the numbers the analysis templates print come
from placeholder values in `tools/synth/params/m1.yaml`, clearly marked and
disclosed by the synthetic-data banner on every page that uses them.

## What you measure {#sec-m1-index-measure}

| Quantity | How | Where it is used later |
|---|---|---|
| Required amplifier gain | Arithmetic against S1's noise floor and quantization | Sizes both amplifiers built in this experiment |
| Non-linearity, hysteresis | Loading/unloading sweep of reference masses on the load cell | Bounds on the load cell's own calibration |
| Creep, zero drift | A held load, and a return to zero after the full sweep | Time-dependent terms no single calibration point can catch |
| Bridge sensitivity ratio | The same masses read through quarter, half and full bridge on the beam | Confirms the [bridge sensitivity relations](handbook.qmd#eq-m1-bridge-configs) and which arrangement cancels what |
| Apparent strain per kelvin | Quarter vs. dummy-compensated half bridge, beam unloaded, at two temperatures | Quantifies what temperature compensation actually buys |
| Beam strain at the gauge, and its uncertainty | Quarter-bridge sweep at the beam tip | [M2](../M2-hall-displacement/index.qmd)'s stiffness cross-check |

: What M1 produces {#tbl-m1-index-outputs}

## Bench {#sec-m1-index-bench}

**Tier 3.** [The cantilever beam rig](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd), a
standalone load cell, an instrumentation amplifier stage for each sensor (see
[the conditioning board](../../hardware/conditioning-board.qmd#sec-cond-inamp)),
strain gauges bonded to the beam in quarter/half/full-bridge wiring, a set of
reference masses, and a way to change the beam's temperature by a known
amount.

**Board.** Any supported board works; nothing here needs streaming timing
quality beyond what [S1](../S1-daq-static/index.qmd) already characterizes.

**Host.** Any — this experiment does not depend on host-timing effects the
way S1/S2/S3 do.

## Reference data {#sec-m1-index-data}

Twenty-four generated runs ship with the experiment, in `data/`:

| File(s) | Contents |
|---|---|
| `load-loading-*`, `load-unloading-*` (10 runs) | Five reference masses, loaded then unloaded, through the standalone load cell |
| `load-creep` | One mass held for 60 s |
| `load-zero-return` | A zero reading taken after the full loading/unloading/creep sequence |
| `bridge-quarter-*` (4), `bridge-half-*` (2), `bridge-full-*` (2) | The same small reference masses at the beam tip, read through each bridge configuration |
| `temp-quarter-cold/-hot`, `temp-half-cold/-hot` (4) | Beam unloaded, quarter vs. half bridge, two bench temperatures |

: Reference data shipped with M1 {#tbl-m1-index-data}

::: {.callout-warning}
## The reference data is synthetic

It is produced by a seeded generator (`tools/synth/m1_strain_load.py`) whose
parameters — including every beam dimension — are plausible placeholders,
not measurements, marked `TODO (Paolo)` in `tools/synth/params/m1.yaml`. It
exists so the analysis templates render, and are checked in continuous
integration, with no bench attached. Every page that uses it says so.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
## Instructor summary {.instructor-note}

Four hours, tier 3, needs S1 as a prerequisite — the in-amp sizing arithmetic
and the four-way load-cell characterization are where the session earns its
extra time over S1. Full notes, expected values, common failures and the
rubric are in the [handbook](handbook.qmd#sec-m1-instructor).
:::
